caption: Figure1. Latent Diffusion Planning. Left: LDP separates the control problem into forecasting future states with a diffusion-based planner, and extracting actions with a diffusion-based inverse dynamics model (IDM). This design enables training on heterogeneous sources of data, including suboptimal data and action-free data. Right: Unlike action imitation methods such as diffusion policy, LDP is based on forecasting a dense temporal sequence of latent states as well as actions. Using powerful diffusion models for both of these objectives enables LDP to have competitive performance to state-of-the-art imitation learning. Further, unlike prior work on forecasting subgoals, LDP predicts a dense temporal sequence of latent states, which enables scalable closed-loop planning.
